commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot Duke -> PDD and add greet/exit behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Renames Duke.java to PDD.java and updates references in README.md and
docs/README.md accordingly. Also updates main() to print a greeting
banner followed by an exit message, per the level-0 requirement to
simply greet the user and exit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Echo user commands and exit on 'bye'
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a read-eval loop using Scanner that echoes each line of input
back to the user, wrapped in divider lines, until the user types
'bye', at which point the exit message is printed and the loop ends.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task list: store commands and support 'list'
commitResults.messageBody:
Non-'list'/'bye' input is now stored as a task and echoed as
'added: <task>'. The 'list' command prints all stored tasks
with 1-based numbering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to mark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Tracks completion status in a parallel List<Boolean>, and adds a
'mark <index>' command to set a task as done. 'list' now shows a
header and each task's status icon ([X]/[ ]). No new classes added,
per the requirement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to unmark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds an 'unmark <index>' command that reverses a task's done status
back to not-done, mirroring the existing 'mark' command. No new
classes added, per the requirement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Introduce Task class to represent tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Extracts task state (description, done status) into a dedicated
Task class in its own file, replacing the parallel List<String>/
List<Boolean> tracking in PDD.java. Task exposes markAsDone(),
markAsNotDone(), and a toString() used for list/mark/unmark output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store tasks in fixed-size Task[100] array instead of ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody:
Per the A-Inheritance increment spec, task storage now uses a plain
Task[100] array with a taskCount tracker instead of List<Task>,
relying on polymorphism (Todo/Deadline/Event references stored as
Task) rather than a collections API. Duplicated 'added' printout
logic across todo/deadline/event/fallback branches is consolidated
into a single addTask helper that returns the updated count.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI test skill/plan, enforce testing workflow, fix missing task type files
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add Todo.java, Deadline.java, Event.java: these were referenced by
  PDD.java since the 'Add support for tracking three types of tasks'
  change but never actually committed, leaving HEAD in a broken
  (non-compiling) state. Committing them now restores a working build.
- Add .claude/skills/test-ui/SKILL.md: a project skill that runs the
  console UI test cases in test/ui-test-plan.md against the compiled
  program, doing exact output comparison, recording a full session
  transcript, and stopping immediately on the first mismatch.
- Add test/ui-test-plan.md: initial verified test cases covering
  greet/exit, adding all three task types + list, mark/unmark, and
  raw (unparsed) date/time strings.
- Update AGENTS.md: after any change to src/main/java/*.java, update
  the UI test plan if needed and invoke the test-ui skill before
  considering the task done.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle user input errors via a custom PDDException
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds PDDException (a checked exception, per the A-Exceptions
extension) and routes command dispatch through try/catch so invalid
input produces a specific, corrective message instead of crashing or
being silently misinterpreted:
- unknown commands
- empty todo/deadline/event descriptions
- deadline missing '/by', event missing '/from' or '/to'
- mark/unmark with a missing, non-numeric, or out-of-range task number

Removes the old fallback that silently added any unrecognized input
as a plain task, since that's now superseded by the unknown-command
error. Adds TC5-TC8 to test/ui-test-plan.md covering these error
paths; all 8 test cases verified passing by manually running the
test-ui skill's procedure end to end.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command; switch task storage to ArrayList<Task>
commitResults.messageBody:
Per the A-Collections extension, replaces the fixed-size Task[100]
array + manual taskCount tracking with a List<Task> (ArrayList),
giving dynamic sizing and built-in add/remove instead of manual
index bookkeeping.

Adds a 'delete <index>' command that reuses the existing
parseTaskIndex helper, so it gets the same missing/non-numeric/
out-of-range error handling already used by mark/unmark.

Adds TC9 to test/ui-test-plan.md covering delete's success path
(matching the spec's example verbatim) and its error paths;
TC1-TC9 all verified passing end to end.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use an enum for command dispatch
commitResults.messageBody:
Per the A-Enums extension, replaces the if/else chain of
command.equals(...) checks with a switch over a new private
Command enum (LIST, MARK, UNMARK, DELETE, TODO, DEADLINE, EVENT),
parsed via Command.valueOf(command.toUpperCase()). Unrecognized
command text still produces the existing unknown-command
PDDException message. Task types (Todo/Deadline/Event) remain
modeled via inheritance rather than an enum, since polymorphic
dispatch is the better fit there.

No behavior change: TC1-TC9 in test/ui-test-plan.md verified
byte-identical before and after.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist tasks to disk automatically (Level 7)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Storage class that saves the task list to ./data/pdd.txt after
every mutating command (mark/unmark/delete/todo/deadline/event), and
loads it back on startup. Task becomes abstract with an abstract
toFileFormat() so each subtype can serialize itself; Storage parses
each line independently and skips (with a warning) any line that
doesn't match the expected format, so a corrupted line doesn't take
down the rest of the save file. Missing file/folder on first run is
treated as an empty task list rather than an error. ./data/ is
gitignored since it's runtime-generated, not source.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse and display deadline/event dates as LocalDate (Level 8)
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline's /by and Event's /from now parse as java.time.LocalDate
instead of being stored as raw strings: input is accepted in
yyyy-MM-dd (ISO) format and displayed as "MMM dd yyyy" (e.g.
Dec 01 2019). Event's /to stays free text since it's usually just a
time-of-day rather than a full date.

Add Task.occursOn(LocalDate), overridden by Deadline/Event, and a new
`on <date>` command that lists every deadline/event occurring on a
given date (stretch goal) without instanceof checks in PDD.

Storage's deadline/event parsing now goes through LocalDate.parse,
reusing the existing corrupted-line skip logic from Level 7: a
pre-Level-8 save file with a non-ISO date string is treated as
corrupted and skipped with a warning rather than crashing the loader.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class for all console I/O (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
PDD.main was mixing command dispatch logic with System.out.println
calls and Scanner reading throughout its body. Move all of that
console I/O into a new Ui class (welcome/goodbye messages, the
divider line, readCommand(), and one show*() method per kind of
response PDD needs to print). PDD now calls Ui methods instead of
printing directly, which is a pure refactor: behavior and output are
unchanged (verified against all 11 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md).

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to wrap the task list (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
PDD.main held a raw List<Task> and had its own free-standing
parseTaskIndex helper for validating 1-based user-typed task numbers.
Wrap the list in a TaskList class that owns add/delete/get/size and
the index-bounds check (toIndex), since that check is really a
TaskList invariant, not a parsing concern. Storage still works on a
plain List<Task> (via TaskList.getTasks()) so it stays unchanged.
Pure refactor: output verified unchanged against all 11 UI test cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class for command-string and date parsing (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
The per-command validation and splitting logic (checking for empty
descriptions, splitting on /by, /from, /to, parsing yyyy-MM-dd dates,
and resolving the command word to an enum) lived inline in each
switch case of PDD.main. Move all of it into a new Parser class:
getCommandWord/getCommandArgs split a raw input line, parseCommandType
resolves the command word, and parseTodo/parseDeadline/parseEvent/
parseOnDate turn the remaining arguments into a ready-to-use Task or
LocalDate (or a PDDException with the right message). PDD.main's
switch cases now just call Parser and act on the result via
Ui/TaskList/Storage. Pure refactor: output verified unchanged against
all 11 UI test cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire PDD as a thin instance coordinator (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
PDD.main was a single static method building and driving its own
Ui/Storage/TaskList locals. Convert PDD to the constructor+run() shape
used elsewhere in the course material: storage/tasks/ui become
instance fields set up in the constructor, main() just instantiates
PDD and calls run(). This completes the minimal A-MoreOOP target
(Ui, TaskList, Parser now hold everything PDD used to do directly).
Pure refactor: output verified unchanged against all 11 UI test cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add abstract Command class (A-MoreOOP stretch goal, step 1/3)
commitResults.messageBody:
First step of the stretch goal: represent each user command as an
object rather than an enum branch. Command declares execute(tasks,
ui, storage) and isExit() (default false, overridden only by
ExitCommand). Not wired into PDD yet — this file is unused until the
concrete Command subclasses (next commit) and Parser.parse (final
commit) exist. Compiles and all 11 UI test cases still pass unchanged
since nothing calls into this class yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add concrete Command subclasses (A-MoreOOP stretch goal, step 2/3)
commitResults.messageBody:
Second step of the stretch goal: one Command subclass per command
type (List/Mark/Unmark/Delete/Todo/Deadline/Event/On/Exit), each
holding just the data it needs and moving the corresponding case body
out of PDD's switch into its execute(). Mark/Unmark/Delete hold the
raw task-number argument and validate it via TaskList.toIndex() at
execute time (bounds depend on the list's state when the command
runs, not when it's parsed); Todo/Deadline/Event/On hold an
already-parsed Task/LocalDate since Parser can build those upfront.
Not wired into PDD yet — still unused until Parser.parse() and the
rewritten PDD.run() (next commit) construct and invoke them. Compiles
and all 11 UI test cases still pass unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire Command objects through Parser and PDD.run() (A-MoreOOP stretch goal, step 3/3)
commitResults.messageBody:
Final step of the stretch goal. Parser gets a public parse(String)
that resolves the command word (now including BYE, so exit is just
another command instead of being special-cased before the loop even
starts) and returns the matching Command, fully constructed:
Mark/Unmark/Delete get the raw task-number text (validated later,
against the list's state at execute time); Todo/Deadline/Event/On get
an already-parsed Task/LocalDate. parseCommandType and the per-type
parse helpers drop to private now that only Parser.parse() calls them.

PDD.run() collapses to the generic loop from the exercise brief: read
-> showLine() -> Parser.parse() -> command.execute(tasks, ui, storage)
-> check isExit(), with showLine() in a finally so it still prints
once per command whether or not it threw. This reproduces the "bye"
output exactly (ExitCommand.execute() prints the goodbye message; the
loop's own showLine() calls around it are unchanged) without a special
case for it. Output verified unchanged against all 11 UI test cases.

This completes A-MoreOOP (minimal target + stretch goal).

commitResults.messageTitle: Update UI test plan's architecture description for A-MoreOOP
commitResults.messageBody:
The intro paragraph still named the pre-refactor file list (Task,
Todo, Deadline, Event, Storage only). Update it to describe the
current collaborators (Ui, Storage, TaskList, Parser, Command
hierarchy) so the test plan's own documentation stays accurate. No
test cases changed — console output is unaffected by A-MoreOOP, as
verified by every iteration's test-ui run.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreOOP: extract OOP structure from PDD.java
commitResults.messageBody:
Pulls the responsibilities that used to live inline in PDD.main into
their own classes: Ui (console I/O), TaskList (the task list and its
invariants), and Parser (command-string/date parsing), leaving PDD as
a thin constructor+run() coordinator (minimal target). Then, as the
stretch goal, represents each user command as a Command object
(ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, TodoCommand,
DeadlineCommand, EventCommand, OnCommand, ExitCommand) so PDD.run()
collapses to the generic read/parse/execute loop from the exercise
brief, with Parser.parse() doing all the work of turning a raw input
line into a ready-to-run Command.

Pure refactor throughout: every one of the 7 iterations was verified
against all 11 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md with no change in
console output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into pdd, pdd.ui, pdd.storage, pdd.parser, pdd.task, pdd.command packages (A-Packages)
commitResults.messageBody:
All 20 classes lived directly in src/main/java with no package. Split
them by responsibility into a pdd package tree, still rooted at
src/main/java (per the exercise's instruction not to make
src/main/java itself part of the package name):

  pdd          PDD.java (entry point), PDDException.java
  pdd.ui        Ui.java
  pdd.storage   Storage.java
  pdd.parser    Parser.java
  pdd.task      Task.java, Todo.java, Deadline.java, Event.java, TaskList.java
  pdd.command   Command.java + the 9 concrete *Command classes

PDDException stays in the root pdd package rather than its own
pdd.exception package, since it's a single small type used by nearly
every other package. Each moved file gets a package declaration and
whatever imports its cross-package references now need.

Task.DISPLAY_DATE_FORMAT widens from protected to public: it's
accessed from Ui.showTasksOn() (pdd.ui), a different package from
Task (pdd.task), and protected only permits same-package or subclass
access. Task's other protected members are only used within pdd.task
(by Task's own subclasses), so they're unaffected.

Also updates the two docs that assumed a flat, unqualified layout:
.claude/skills/test-ui/SKILL.md's compile/run commands (now compile
recursively and run the qualified class pdd.PDD), and
test/ui-test-plan.md's intro paragraph describing the architecture.

Pure refactor: verified with a fresh recursive javac compile and all
11 UI test cases in test/ui-test-plan.md producing byte-identical
output against java -cp <dir> pdd.PDD.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Packages: organize classes into Java packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Groups the 20 classes under src/main/java (kept as the source root, as
required) into a pdd package tree by responsibility: pdd (entry point
+ the shared PDDException), pdd.ui, pdd.storage, pdd.parser, pdd.task,
pdd.command. Task.DISPLAY_DATE_FORMAT widens to public since Ui, now
in a different package, needs it. Pure refactor, verified against all
11 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md with a fresh recursive-javac compile
and java -cp <dir> pdd.PDD.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch add-gradle-support: add Gradle wrapper and build.gradle (A-Gradle step 1)
commitResults.messageBody:
Fetches and merges origin/add-gradle-support (the course's separately
provided Gradle scaffolding branch) into master, per the A-Gradle
exercise's Step 1. Since this branch diverged from master's history
far upstream of the PDD rename, package reorganization, and
AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md additions, the merge only brings in the
Gradle-specific files with no conflicts: build.gradle, the Gradle
wrapper (gradlew, gradlew.bat, gradle/wrapper/*), and nothing else

build.gradle as merged in still points at the old template's

commitResults.messageTitle: Point Gradle build at this project's actual entry point (A-Gradle step 2)
commitResults.messageBody:
build.gradle came in from the add-gradle-support branch still
configured for the original course template (mainClass
seedu.duke.Duke, shadowJar output duke.jar) - neither exists in this
project, which uses pdd.PDD (package pdd, per A-Packages). Update
both to match: mainClass = 'pdd.PDD', shadowJar archiveFileName =
'pdd.jar'.

Verified `./gradlew build` succeeds and `./gradlew run` (with stdin
piped in) produces the same output as running the compiled class
directly - Gradle can now build and run the chatbot, satisfying

commitResults.messageTitle: Switch test-ui skill to Gradle compile/run commands (A-Gradle)
commitResults.messageBody:
The skill's own notes already flagged this: "no build.gradle present
as of this writing... If a build tool is later added to the project,
prefer its equivalent compile/run commands instead." Now that it has
been (previous two commits), switch step 2 to `./gradlew compileJava`
and step 3b to running directly against
`build/classes/java/main` (kept as a raw `java -cp` invocation per
test case, rather than `./gradlew run` each time, to avoid paying
Gradle's own startup cost 11 times over).

Verified: all 11 cases in test/ui-test-plan.md still pass
byte-identical output when compiled and run this way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for the core non-UI logic (A-JUnit)
commitResults.messageBody:
Goes past the minimal target (2 methods in 2 classes) to cover the
codebase's highest-value logic with JUnit 5, run via `./gradlew test`
(JUnit deps and useJUnitPlatform() were already wired up in
build.gradle by A-Gradle):

- pdd.task.{Todo,Deadline,Event}Test: toString()/toFileFormat()/
  occursOn() for each task type, including the done/not-done and
  date-matching branches.
- pdd.task.TaskListTest: toIndex()'s bounds/format validation (valid,
  non-numeric, zero, out-of-range) and add()/delete().
- pdd.parser.ParserTest: Parser.parse() for every command type,
  exercised by executing the returned Command against a fresh
  TaskList and asserting the resulting state (Command's parsed fields
  are deliberately private with no getters, so behavior rather than
  internal state is what's verified), plus its error paths (empty
  description, missing '/by', invalid date, unknown command word).
- pdd.storage.StorageTest: missing-file load, a full save-then-load
  round trip across all three task types and their done status, and
  that a corrupted line is skipped without losing the valid lines
  around it — using @TempDir so nothing touches the real ./data/pdd.txt.

Left out of scope: pdd.ui.Ui (println wrappers with no real logic)
and the pdd.command.* classes (thin execute() delegations already
exercised both here, indirectly, through ParserTest, and by the
existing end-to-end test/ui-test-plan.md suite).

Verified: `./gradlew test` — all 33 tests pass. Also re-ran the full
11-case UI suite from test/ui-test-plan.md to confirm no regressions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc to all remaining public classes and methods (A-JavaDoc)
commitResults.messageBody:
Fills the gaps left after earlier increments: class-level docs for
PDDException, Task (abstract), Todo, Deadline, Event; constructor
docs everywhere (PDDException, PDD, Storage, TaskList, Task, Todo,
Deadline, Event, and the *Command subclasses that take constructor
arguments); and method docs for PDD.run()/main(),
TaskList.size()/get()/add()/delete(), and Task's remaining accessors
(getStatusIcon, getDescription, markAsDone, markAsNotDone).

toString() overrides are left undocumented (exact-match override of
Object's contract, exempt per the SE-EDU Java standard). Deadline's
and Event's occursOn() overrides get {@inheritDoc}, since Task's own
doc for occursOn() already states the general contract accurately.
Concrete Command subclasses' execute() overrides are likewise exempt
(exact-match override of Command.execute()'s contract) - only their
constructors needed new docs.

Pure documentation change: `./gradlew build` and `./gradlew test`
both still pass with no code behavior touched.

Tag: A-JavaDoc

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword (Level 9)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `find <keyword>`, which lists every task whose description
contains the keyword, case-insensitively (not specified by the
exercise; chosen for usability, matching common expectations for a
search command) - mirroring the exercise's own example output
("Here are the matching tasks in your list:").

- TaskList.findMatching(String): new query alongside its existing
  add/delete/get operations.
- Ui.showMatchingTasks(List<Task>): same shape as showTaskList but
  with the "matching tasks" header.
- Parser: new FIND case in CommandType/parse(), and parseFindKeyword()

- FindCommand: the new Command subclass tying the above together.

Tests: TaskListTest covers findMatching's match/no-match/case-
insensitive cases; ParserTest covers the find command and its empty-
keyword error. New TC12 in test/ui-test-plan.md exercises `find`
end-to-end (mirroring the exercise's own example).

Verified: `./gradlew test` (all JUnit tests pass) and all 12 cases in
test/ui-test-plan.md, including the new TC12, produce the expected
output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CodingStandard: adopt SE-EDU Java/Git conventions

Adds two project skills (seedu-java-coding-standard,

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-JavaDoc: Javadoc all remaining public classes/methods
Merge branch-Level-9: add find command to search tasks by keyword
Add Checkstyle to detect coding style violations (A-CheckStyle)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adopts Checkstyle as an automated, objective check that the project
follows the Java coding standard already documented in the
/seedu-java-coding-standard skill. The skill guides how code is
written; Checkstyle is a verification step (runnable via Gradle, and
usable in CI) that catches drift regardless of who or what wrote the
code, so the two are complementary rather than redundant.

- Copy config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml and suppressions.xml from the
  SE-EDU AddressBook Level 3 reference project, which targets the same
  intermediate Java coding standard this repo follows.
- Add the 'checkstyle' Gradle plugin (toolVersion 14.1.0, matching
  AB3's current pin) to build.gradle.
- Fix violations found by `./gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest`:
  - Re-indent the switch statements in Parser.parse and
    Storage.parseTask so case labels sit one level deeper than the
    switch, per the config's caseIndent=4 (Indentation).
  - Collapse a wrapped assertThrows(...) call in ParserTest onto one
    line so its lambda's opening parenthesis isn't left at the start
    of a wrapped line (SeparatorWrap).
  - Suppress AbbreviationAsWordInName for PDD.java/PDDException.java:
    "PDD" is this project's product name, not an abbreviation to
    split into words (comparable to AB3 exempting its own naming
    choices via suppressions.xml).

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-CheckStyle: add Checkstyle to detect style violations
Add a JavaFX GUI to the chatbot (Level-10)
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot has only had a console UI so far. This increment adds a
JavaFX GUI, following the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial's Parts 1-4 pattern
(Launcher workaround, programmatic layout, then FXML + controller),
while keeping the console text UI working — it's still what makes
the core logic easy to test via JUnit and the text-based test-ui
skill.

- Add pdd.gui.Launcher/Main/MainWindow/DialogBox and their FXML
  views, following the tutorial's structure closely rather than an
  ad hoc layout.
- Make pdd.ui.Ui's output destination pluggable (a Consumer<String>
  writer, defaulting to System.out::println) instead of hardcoding
  System.out.println in every show* method. This lets a GUI-mode Ui
  collect the same lines into a string instead of printing them,
  without changing a single Command subclass.
- Add PDD.getResponse(String) (parses and executes one command,

Use varargs to collapse Ui's multi-line prints (A-Varargs)
commitResults.messageBody:
Several Ui.show* methods printed a small, fixed set of lines via
consecutive writer.accept(...) calls (showWelcome: 3, showMarked/
showUnmarked: 2 each, showDeleted/showAdded: 3 each) - exactly the
case varargs is for: a fixed, inline argument list known at each
call site, not a runtime-sized collection (which is why
showTaskList/showTasksOn/showMatchingTasks, which loop over a
List<Task> of unknown size, are left as-is).

Add a private `print(String... lines)` helper and use it at those
call sites instead. Private and additive - no public API changes,
so output is byte-for-byte unchanged (verified via the JUnit suite
and all 12 test-ui cases).
